key_insight: IR-Flow uses Rectified Flow to create multilevel data distribution flows that combine the speed of discriminative single-step restoration with the fine-detail reconstruction of generative multi-step methods, reducing noise–residual coupling while keeping sampling efficient.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between fast but detail-poor discriminative restorers and high-quality but slow/noise-coupled generative samplers, enabling efficient restoration with sharper, more faithful details.
method: Build multilevel data-distribution flows that expand and structure degraded-to-clean image mappings across scales.
Apply Rectified Flow inference to iteratively correct samples while avoiding heavy multi-step noise-residual coupling, enabling faster, more accurate sampling.
Unify discriminative expectation-based objectives and generative flow-based sampling into a single framework to obtain both computational efficiency and improved fine-detail recovery.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical restoration strategy that improves perceptual fidelity without the high computational cost of traditional generative sampling, making high-quality image restoration more usable in real applications and pipelines.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: discriminative (single-step) vs generative (multi-step) vs IR-Flow (multilevel rectified flow) showing trade-offs

paper_title: IR-Flow: Bridging Discriminative and Generative Image Restoration via Rectified Flow
paper_authors: Zihao Fan, Xin Lu, Jie Xiao, Dong Li, Jie Huang
